generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the benefits of learning by doing are clear. A placement in a clinic or school gives you authentic experience of how psychology is practised, not just how it is written up. You build practical skills, such as interviewing or running an assessment, by using them. You grow in confidence with real clients and real data, and you begin to see yourself as a future psychologist, which is exactly what employers and training routes look for.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students finish the same placement in a mental health service and are asked what they got out of it.

Tom says it was fine, but cannot point to anything gained. He did the tasks without noticing what they taught, and comes away with hours completed but no sense of having developed.

Amara can name what the placement gave her: real skills used for the first time, more confidence with clients, and a clearer idea of the career she wants in clinical psychology. She sees the experience as something that developed her, not just time served.

Both did the same placement. Only Amara recognised its benefits: the authentic experience, the skills, the confidence and the sense of direction it offered.
generatedProse.summary: Practice- and work-based learning in psychology is valuable because it offers authentic experience of real practice, builds practical skills by using them, grows your confidence, and helps you see yourself as a future psychologist. You can now describe these benefits and recognise them in a student's experience. With a clear picture of what this learning is, the forms it takes and why it matters, you are ready to make the most of it when it comes.

check.body: In the worked example, what showed that Amara had gained from the placement?

items.text: She could name real skills, more confidence, and a clearer sense of the career she wanted.
She completed more hours than Tom did.
She said it was fine but could point to nothing.

feedback.correct: That's right. Being able to name skills, confidence and a clearer direction shows the experience developed her.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara could point to as having gained.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara had gained because she could name real skills, more confidence and a clearer sense of the career she wanted.
